statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month is near 29,637 (+0.24%) inside a 29,530.50-29,682.50 band roughly 0.51% wide that has now contained about twelve hours of trade, and the session high has still not been retested. Tail holds at 5 because the price path remains contained and two-way, and because the oil impulse is flat rather than building: Brent is $96.61 (+0.35%) against a $97.58 peak earlier this morning and WTI is $91.41 (-0.07%). Stress rises one point to 55 on Brent firming off its intraday low, an unresolved Iranian restricted-zone threat in the Persian Gulf after weekend US strikes on three Iranian tankers, global long-end yields at multi-year highs, holiday-thinned depth with US cash equity and Treasury markets closed for Labor Day, and roughly 60% implied odds of a 25bp Fed hike on 15-16 September. Confidence holds at 85 on two current futures feeds with an explicit session range, live Brent and WTI prints, live European cash levels, and verified holiday, exchange and data-release schedules.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold in every hour of this outlook. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the shortened Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than spread across the whole session. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold their overnight band into a shortened Labor Day session as oil steadies near $96.60 and US cash markets stay shut
body:
The price path is the strongest evidence this hour and it argues for a low tail value. The band from 29,530.50 to 29,682.50 has now contained roughly twelve hours of trade, about 0.51% wide. The high was made, rejected and has not been retested; NQ is near 29,637, up 0.24%, sitting inside the band rather than pressing either edge. That is containment with working retracements, which is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency that overwhelms a mean-reversion approach.

Oil is elevated but no longer impulsive. Brent is $96.61, up 0.35% on the day but below the $97.58 peak reached in the early European hours, and WTI is $91.41, marginally lower. Last week Brent gained about 9.3% and WTI about 9.7% on renewed US-Iran fighting; this session the premium is holding rather than compounding. The US struck three Iranian tankers over the weekend, destroying one, in retaliation for ballistic missile attacks on US Navy warships, and Tehran has threatened restricted maritime zones in the Persian Gulf. The US Energy Secretary said millions of barrels were still moving through the Strait of Hormuz. A geopolitical premium that stabilises intraday raises Stress without supplying the Tail amplifier.

Cross-asset alignment is absent. NQ is bid while the pan-European STOXX 600 is down about 0.1%, the DAX 0.14% and the FTSE 100 0.12%, with the FTSE MIB higher and Asia-Pacific closed broadly up. VIX last printed 15.03. US Treasury cash is closed for the holiday, so the H.15 curve as of 3 September, with the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, is the latest available reference and cannot move today. Divergence of this kind normally lifts uncertainty rather than tail risk.

The macro backdrop is what keeps Stress elevated at 55. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1%, and following Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address that has left implied odds of a 25bp hike on 15-16 September near 60%. PPI lands Thursday and CPI Friday, and the ECB is widely expected to raise rates this week. Under the calibration used here an unresolved catalyst stack of this kind maps to Stress and to Confidence, not to Tail, until an observed price path establishes retracement failure.

Structure of the day matters more than usual. NYSE, Nasdaq and the US bond market are closed for Labor Day, CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC and restart at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. The flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covers the European cash close running into that halt, when depth thins from both venues at once and a headline impulse would be poorly absorbed. The 22:00 UTC restart carries a second, narrower conditional risk because five closed hours concentrate any accumulated news into a single repricing. Neither is an observed condition; both are conditional allowances, and every hour in this outlook remains inside the low tail band.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased back to 5 once that restart proved orderly, lifted to 7 as the overnight high extended, and settled at 6 then 5 as that high was retraced and left unretested. Stress ranged from 54 to 60, peaking at 60 into the Sunday close before holding the mid-50s across the Asian session and the European morning. Confidence stayed in a narrow 84 to 86 band. Dominant mode was normal in every available hour, and no hour in the window mapped above EA_ON.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the European morning and a holiday afternoon traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session into the European cash open. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour and the next, 6 across the late European morning and the holiday afternoon where thinned depth meets no US cash backstop, 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 falling to 4 across the closed hours, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for reopen-gap risk, and 7 easing to 6 through the Tuesday Asian session before returning to 7 at the European handover. Stress runs 55 to 58 while the venue is open, steps down to 46 to 48 across the halt, and returns to 55 to 57 from the restart onward as the ECB decision, Thursday PPI, Friday CPI and the 15-16 September FOMC come into view. Confidence eases from 85 to 76 as the horizon lengthens. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green.
